test_title: SSC CPO Tier-II Previous Year Paper (Held On: 8th November 2021)
subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

__To keeping__ the photo in front of her, Jia drew the picture.
solution:
The correct answer is '**Keeping**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given above sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• In the above-given sentence, '**To keeping**' will be replaced by ‘Keeping’.
 
• As per the general rule, "**keeping**" is used **as a gerund** which makes "**keeping warm**" **a noun phrase**.
 
• "**to keep**" is the **infinitive form**, wherein "**to**" is simply **part of the infinitive**. So, one might say that "**to keep warm**" is a **sentence adverb**.
 
• **both are correct**, but **they differ grammatically**.
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• ***Keeping/to keep **her voice conversational, she asked him without looking up. (correct)*
 
• ***To keeping** her voice conversational, she asked him without looking up. (incorrect)*
 
 
 
• ​Here in the given above sentence, '**To keeping**' is used**, **which is wrong according to the rule.
 
• According to the explanation and example that are given above, ‘Keeping’ is the most appropriate substitute to the underlined segment.

**Correct sentence:** *Keeping the photo in front of her, Jia drew the picture.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• **"Being kept":** This use of passive voice makes it unclear who is keeping the photo in front of Jia.

 
 
• Is someone else placing it there for her?
 
• Passive voice is not appropriate in this context, because it shifts the focus away from what Jia is doing.
 
• This form would suggest that the photo somehow remained in front of Jia as she drew, but does not indicate that she herself placed or kept it there.
 
 
 
• **"To have kept"**: Using "to have" followed by the past participle of a verb is used to form the perfect infinitive.
 
 
• In this context, it would suggest that the action of Jia keeping the photo in front of her occurred (and finished) before she drew the picture.
 
• It is not the right tense in this context.
